original_test_intent: Verify the fan board's I2C management devices and responses while proving fan control, tachometer telemetry and platform thermal protection remain healthy.
original_method: The Master supplies only a missing-spec placeholder. Until the fan-board controller, mux, addresses, permitted reads, expected values and thermal recovery are defined, the agent must not access the bus.
manual_activity: Thermal/platform owners must identify FAN_BD, document controller/mux/address ownership and approve non-disruptive reads plus fan/temperature stop thresholds.
required_inputs: Fan-controller, tachometer, PWM and sensor address/register map
Baseline duty, RPM and temperature limits
safety_requirements: Do not scan every I2C adapter
Do not probe unknown fan-control registers
Do not change PWM, mode or watchdog state
Confirm adequate cooling before any approved access
Continuously preserve RPM and temperature evidence
Stop on fan-speed, thermal, BMC or bus anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Perform no scan, read or fan-control operation
Require a fresh case review after inputs
engineer_actions: Provide independent thermal recovery and aborts

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The command searches every host-visible adapter instead of selecting the FAN_BD controller/mux and cannot tell fan-control registers from benign identity endpoints. It also truncates the map and collects no synchronous RPM, PWM or temperature evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED: define the fan-board topology and register-level read allowlist with thermal limits before any I2C command.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The FAN_BD scope and two-minute estimates remain intact; no fan count, bus, address or register is assumed.

modernized_recommendation.status: PENDING FAN-BOARD I2C AND THERMAL CONTRACT
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After specification approval, use the owning BMC/OOB interface to read allowlisted identity and status registers on the exact FAN_BD branch while sampling fan RPM/PWM, temperatures and BMC events before, during and after the bounded access.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Binds bus access to the physical fan board and a thermal-safety oracle rather than generic address discovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Finding an address does not prove correct fan-resource mapping, valid tach/PWM data or unchanged cooling control.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Fan controllers can share registers for status and control, and bus contention or an unsafe transaction could impair cooling; independent shutdown/recovery is essential.

project_override_considerations: Treat FAN_BD I2C as BMC/platform-management scope and require the exact BMC controller/bus, target addresses, fan-resource map, vendor procedure and expected output.
expected_evidence: Approved FAN_BD specification and fresh review
Complete allowlisted raw responses mapped to physical fans
Synchronized RPM, PWM, tach fault and temperature baseline/during/final data
BMC SEL/SDR/sensor plus OS thermal evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: No contradictory instructions are present; the required procedure and criterion are wholly absent behind a follow-up-spec reference.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The fan-board map and safe register semantics determine whether a transaction is an observation or a thermal-control hazard. They cannot be inferred from i2c-tools or supplied as a generic user confirmation.

engineering_decision_request.question: Define Functionality row 1803 Wistron-HW-00005-V003 I2C FAN_BD: board/revision and BMC/OOB owner, controller/mux/bus/address map, fan/PWM/tach/sensor register allowlist, expected resource/value matrix, thermal abort thresholds, monitoring and independent cooling/power recovery; preserve Master placeholders and require fresh review.

review_improvement: Elevates the missing fan-controller transaction and thermal oracle to a hard blocker instead of treating i2c-tools plus approval as sufficient.
independent_technical_reasoning: Cooling control is not a passive discovery domain: a probe reaching the wrong register or contending with the BMC can change fan behavior or obscure tach telemetry. The source identifies no route or resource matrix, so an address response would neither prove the named board nor establish safe thermal behavior. Execution must wait for register-level semantics.
